title: Finite-sum monotone root finding with randomized linear-span algorithms

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: The operator $F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n F_i$ is monotone, meaning $\langle F(u)-F(v),u-v\rangle\ge0$. Componentwise monotonicity is not assumed.

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.

model.parameter_domain_description: $R$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $n$: positive integer. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table; additional accuracy and dimension conditions appear in each regime.
description_paragraphs: The condition $F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ holds. The average $F$ is monotone; individual components need not be monotone.
The public initial point is $z_0=0$. A root $z^\star\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $F(z^\star)=0$ and $\|z^\star\|_2\le R$.
To match the output notation of the inclusion problem, fix the set-valued operator $G(z)=\{0\}$. The returned graph element must be $\widehat g=0$; there is no separate unknown $G$.

public_inputs: Public inputs include dimension $d$ and $R$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, and $n$, together with the stated initial-point and feasible-domain information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, or matrices are not revealed.

output.feasibility: Return $(\widehat z,\widehat g)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ with $\widehat g\in G(\widehat z)$. In this slice G=0, so $\widehat g=0$ is required.
output.allowed_postprocessing: arbitrary measurable postprocessing; unqueried output permitted unless restriction says otherwise
output.certificate_requirement: Return $(\widehat z,\widehat g)$, with $\widehat g\in G(\widehat z)$. This root-finding slice fixes $G=0$, hence $\widehat g=0$.
description_paragraphs: Return $(\widehat{z},\widehat{g})\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d$ and ensure $\widehat{g}\in G(\widehat{z})$. Here $G=0$, so $\widehat{g}=0$.
Unqueried outputs are permitted, but remain subject to the stated linear-span condition.

description_paragraphs: Under the present condition $G(z)=\{0\}$, the source notation $\|F(\widehat z)+\widehat g\|_2$ is exactly the root residual used here.

description_paragraphs: One $F_i(z)$ call counts once in $N_{\rm component}$; a complete mean requires $n$ calls.

Use expected work on the worst instance. The algorithm stops almost surely, with call count $\tau$ satisfying $\sup_I\mathbb{E}[\tau]\le N$. This does not require every execution path to finish within $N$ calls.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.
